body.heading: Guess before you look it up
paragraphs: When something puzzles you, resist the instant search. First, make your best guess about how it might work: what parts it needs, what energy it uses, what could go wrong with it. Draw it if you can.
The guess matters even when it is wrong. It gives your mind hooks, so the real explanation, when you find it, sticks to something instead of sliding off.

body.heading: Then check, and enjoy the gap
paragraphs: Now look it up or ask someone who knows. Compare the real mechanism with your guess. The differences are where the learning lives, and they are often more interesting than the answer alone.
Keep a running list of things you have wondered about: how traffic lights decide, why bread rises, how a zip works. It is a curriculum you wrote yourself, which is the most motivating kind.

takeaway: Guess first, check second, and keep a list of things you wonder about.
